title: Development of a Serial Dilution Technique for Obtaining Monoclonal Cell Populations
protocol: Transfect cells using Lipofectamine 2000.
Observe Green Fluorescent Protein (GFP) expression approximately 48 to 72 hours post-transfection.
Monitor cell proliferation and clone formation under a stereomicroscope.
Wait for single cells in each well to proliferate into a clone of approximately 40 cells over 10-12 days.
Seed 3.5-4×10^6 cells per well in a 6-well culture plate containing DMEM devoid of any antibiotics the day before transfection.
Supplement 250 μl Opti-MEM medium with 10 μl Lipofectamine in separate 1.5 ml microtubes and incubate for 20-25 minutes at room temperature.
Gently pipette and mix the vector and Lipofectamine, then transfer the mixture into plates.
Replace the Opti-MEM medium with complete growth medium (DMEM, 10% FBS, 1% penicillin/streptomycin) 4-6 hours following transfection.
Trypsinize the cells and transfer them to a sterile 15ml falcon.
Pellet the cells via centrifugation at 1500 rpm for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the cells in a 1 ml complete growth media.
Analyze cellular viability using the Trypan blue method.
Count viable cells via Neobar chamber.
Isolate and resuspend 10^6 cells in 1 ml growth medium.
Transfer 100 μl of cell suspension to a new flask containing 900 μl medium to dilute by a ratio of 1:10, resulting in a suspension of 10^5 cells per ml.
Continue transferring 100 μl from each subsequent dilution to fresh flasks with 900 μl medium until reaching a population of 10^3 cells per flask.
Transfer 100 μl of the previous step’s result to 96-well plates.
Incubate the cells at 37°C for 6-7 days without any disturbance.
Passage cells into 48-well plates once desired cellular confluency is reached.
Continue passaging cells step-wise into 24, 12, and 6 well plates as the process progresses.
Extract DNA from each well.
Amplify extracted DNA by PCR.
Ligate PCR product into TOPO cloning vector to separate two alleles of every single cell.
Screen and analyze DNA fragments by sequencing.
